indicators.note: someone who has lost the plot is in disarray, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone flies off the handle and starts shouting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost' tells you to rearrange HISRAG. 'Loud' here describes colours or clothes, not noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud clothing is gaudy and showy, the same as garish.

clue.text: Get nice ground on the origin of species from this?

definitions.text: Get nice ground on the origin of species from this?

indicators.note: ground as in milled or crushed, so the letters are broken down and remixed
the origin of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of species is used

explanation.surface: A question about what lies behind Darwin's famous book on how species arose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges GETNICE; 'origin of' gives S, the first letter of 'species', which goes on the end. The whole clue also hints at the field that studies heredity.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of heredity explains how inherited traits give rise to new kinds of living things.

parts.note: rare can mean excellent, as in rare talent

indicators.note: trained means put into new shape, so the letters of SENs are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shortage of good qualified nurses.
explanation.walkthrough: SENs are State Enrolled Nurses, an old British nursing grade. 'trained' rearranges SENS into NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarcity is the state of being seldom found, which is what rareness names.

indicators.note: to capture is to hold inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: statues are sculptures

explanation.surface: Statues are placed so as to catch the sunlight.
explanation.definitionFit: Positions in society or rankings are standings, which are statuses.

parts.note: the answer to 9 across means par or standard, and typical is a synonym of that

explanation.surface: A cross-reference saying one entry is strange.
explanation.walkthrough: Look up 9 across first: its answer (normal) is replaced by the synonym TYPICAL, and A goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something odd departs from the usual pattern, which is what atypical means.

indicators.note: two calls for the piece to appear twice in a row

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Two cats belong to a jazz drummer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom-tom is a hand-beaten drum used in jazz kits.

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: contorted means twisted out of shape, so the letters of grin are rearranged

explanation.surface: Father pulls a twisted grin while shaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaving is a thin slice cut off, like a piece of peel.

parts.note: reads like a batsman hitting a four, but is a line marked (scored) on a cricket pitch where the batsman stands

explanation.surface: A cricketer has just hit a four.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a boundary is a hit for four; here 'scored' means marked, and the boundary is a painted line on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The batting line in cricket is a white mark the batsman must stay behind to avoid being stumped.

indicators.note: putting things to order rearranges them, so the letters of lattes are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Ordering coffees in a trendy café.
explanation.definitionFit: Newest styles are fashionable ones, so the most recent is in vogue.

clue.text: Australian golfer almost got line for par

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Greg Norman is an Australian golfer

explanation.surface: Greg Norman nearly made his putt for par.
explanation.definitionFit: Par means the usual standard, as in below par.

clue.text: Appearing to join forces in hospital department

indicators.note: in places the word for joining forces inside the department

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
to merge is to join forces

explanation.surface: Two teams combine in a hospital unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something coming into view or existence is emerging, just appearing.

clue.text: Air increase to improve an engine's performance

parts.note: an air is a tune
up can mean increase, as in up the price

explanation.surface: A mechanic boosting the intake of air to make a motor run better.
explanation.definitionFit: A service to adjust an engine so it runs more efficiently.

clue.text: Those people stop, oddly, and call for help

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of stop, the first and third

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal

explanation.surface: Some people halt and cry for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' gives SO from STOP (letters one and three).
explanation.definitionFit: So-and-sos are unnamed persons, referred to vaguely or with contempt.

clue.text: Clean mark on most of pool after spilling ash

indicators.note: after puts the shuffled ash before the other pieces
spilling scatters the letters of ash so they land in a new order

parts.note: M is short for mark, the old German currency

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter of the word pool

explanation.surface: Cleaning a stain by the pool after ash has spilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilling' rearranges ASH into SHA; 'after' puts that first; 'most of' trims POOL to POO.
explanation.definitionFit: To shampoo a carpet or hair is to wash it.

clue.text: Heads off one hostile military unit that shows resistance

indicators.note: heads are first letters, so the opening letter of each of these words is taken

explanation.surface: Picking off the leaders of an enemy army unit that fights back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads off' takes the first letters of 'one hostile military'; 'unit' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit of electrical resistance is named after Georg Ohm.

clue.text: After cocaine he was disturbed and kind of nuts

indicators.note: after places the shuffled letters behind the C

parts.note: C is slang for cocaine

indicators.note: disturbed letters are jumbled, so he was is rearranged

explanation.surface: After taking cocaine he was unsettled and a bit crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges HEWAS into ASHEW, which follows C.
explanation.definitionFit: The kidney-shaped cashew is one variety of edible nut.

indicators.note: the letters of How change to become something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone asking what it takes to qualify in medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of HOW names the time-travelling Doctor of the long-running BBC series.
explanation.definitionFit: The Doctor in the BBC science-fiction show is known as Doctor Who.

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter of guests

explanation.surface: Welcoming visitors on a timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: To receive something is to obtain or be given it.

indicators.note: from signals the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A polish worthy of a gleam.
explanation.definitionFit: A shimmer is a soft, wavering gleam of light.

clue.text: He'll provide you with the ordered lattes

definitions.text: He'll provide you with the ordered lattes

parts.words: He'll provide you with the ordered lattes
parts.note: reads like a waiter bringing coffee, but ordered lattes rearranges to the most recent news, which a journalist supplies

explanation.surface: A waiter brings the coffees you asked for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered lattes' is an anagram of LATEST, as in 8 down: the person who brings you the latest is a news writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist gathers and delivers fresh news stories.

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, used on clothing labels
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
late can mean former, as once does

explanation.surface: A huge policeman of old gives a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: To osculate is the formal or jocular word for to kiss.

parts.note: blue means smutty or obscene, as in blue jokes
to give someone a bell is British slang for phoning them

explanation.surface: Someone making a dirty phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: The wild hyacinth is a British name for this woodland flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild hyacinth is a spring woodland flower, an example of the definition.

indicators.note: processing reworks raw material, so the letters of a steel are rearranged

explanation.surface: A factory where steel is produced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory but is a prickly flower head.
explanation.definitionFit: The teasel is a thistle-like flower once used for raising the nap on cloth.

indicators.note: some means part of, so the letters come from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A procession of people at a funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A cortege is a train of attendants accompanying someone, a protective retinue.

clue.text: Virtuous — very-with half the time for ordered lattes

indicators.note: ordered rearranges the letters, with one taken away first

parts.note: lattes holds two Ts, two times; half of them means one T

explanation.surface: Someone abstemious orders coffee half the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half the time' takes one of the two Ts out of LATTES and 'ordered' rearranges the rest, LATES, into ESTAL after V.
explanation.definitionFit: Vestal virgins were chaste priestesses of Rome, so the adjective means pure.

indicators.note: wearing means being worn by, so the trainee sits inside

parts.note: spotted means seen
AT is short for administrative trainee

explanation.surface: A trainee clerk dressed in polka dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Sateen is a glossy cotton fabric woven like satin.

definitions.meaning: a book of the Old Testament
an occupation or line of work

explanation.definitionFit: Job is a biblical book about a suffering man, and a job is an occupation or line of employment.

indicators.note: after puts the broken leg behind the dance

parts.note: a jig is a lively dance

indicators.note: broke means smashed into pieces, so the letters of leg are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone broke a leg after a lively dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To jiggle is to move with short quick jerks.

clue.text: Unusual reactions when head of theatre drops script

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters are put into an unusual order
the head of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An odd response when a theatre director drops a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' removes T, the first letter of 'theatre' ('head of'), from REACTIONS; 'Unusual' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an outline or screenplay for a film or play.

clue.text: Spiral volume Electrical Trades Union returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the union's initials are read backwards

parts.note: ETU is the initials of the Electrical Trades Union

explanation.surface: A union sends back a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A volute is a spiral scroll, as on an Ionic column capital.

clue.text: Ought we to be worried about current best?

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled words go round the current
worried letters are fretted into a new order

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Should we fret about the power supply?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be worried' rearranges OUGHTWE; 'about' wraps those letters around I.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to beat them, to exceed them in value or weight.

indicators.note: wretched suggests a sorry state, so the letters of after are mangled

explanation.surface: A miserable downpour following sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' looks like rain but is a verb: to rain bullets on.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to rake with gunfire from the air, a hail of bullets.

parts.note: a tale is a tall story
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A new lad tells a tall tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Practised means skilled, gifted with ability.

indicators.note: without means outside, so the shuffled letters go around a
criminal means bent or crooked, so the letters of older are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old offender escapes a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: rearranged OLDER goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful experience, a test of endurance.
